info.title: Traigent Backend Agent Readiness Fleet Posture Routes
info.description: The server-computed fleet debt/verdict view for a project. A separate endpoint module because agent_readiness_endpoints.json's path set is pinned by test_endpoint_inventory_registers_project_scoped_read_and_target_routes (same convention as agent_posture_endpoints.json).

get.summary: List every project Agent's computed debt items, verdict and validate-first ranking
get.description: Auth identical to the portfolio route: require_resource_read_access(ResourceType.AGENT, collection=True) + project_role_required('viewer'). Tenant/project are taken from the canonical auth context only, never from headers or query parameters. No request body. Paging mirrors the portfolio list route's page/per_page parameters (agent_readiness_endpoints.json); per_page shares the portfolio route's maximum of 100. Rows are ordered exactly as the portfolio list route orders its full portfolio before paging (AgentReadinessService.list_portfolio, TraigentBackend src/services/analytics/agent_readiness_service.py:1143-1145/1222-1224, called from fleet_posture_service.py's get_fleet_posture): evaluation-progress stage ascending (NO_RUNS, then RUNS_RECORDED, then EVALUATION_COMPLETED), then last-activity ascending with nulls first, then agent_id ascending as the final tiebreaker; the new filters narrow this same ordered set and do not change the ordering. The optional agent_id query parameter restricts the response to one Agent's row and, when present, makes page/per_page paging moot (see agent_id). Five additional optional filters -- verdict, stage, deployment_stage (each repeatable: OR within the parameter), search (substring on agent_name), and include_project_summary -- combine with each other and with agent_id by AND, and all of them apply BEFORE pagination: pagination.total/pagination.total_pages are always the FILTERED count, never the project's unfiltered total. A comma-separated value for a repeatable filter (verdict/stage/deployment_stage) is REJECTED, not parsed as a list -- each value must be its own query-string occurrence (e.g. ?verdict=STAY&verdict=INTERVENE_QUALITY); a REPEATED IDENTICAL value in a repeatable filter (e.g. ?verdict=STAY&verdict=STAY) is accepted and de-duplicated, behaving the same as a single occurrence. Any unknown/invalid filter value, a duplicate occurrence of the singleton search or include_project_summary parameters, or an out-of-bounds search yields the existing 400 envelope (see the route's 400 response) with the offending value never echoed. The agent_id no-existence-oracle privacy invariant (see agent_id) is unchanged by any of these filters: an unknown/inaccessible agent_id still returns the same 200 empty-fleet shape, never 404, regardless of what else is requested. ENHANCED PATH, precisely defined: a request is on the enhanced path if AND ONLY IF at least one of the following holds -- verdict, stage or deployment_stage is present (any occurrence); search is present AND non-blank after trimming; or include_project_summary=true. A request with none of these (including one with a blank/whitespace-only search, or an explicit include_project_summary=false) is on the pre-existing, unbounded page-only path and is NOT subject to the 500-caller-visible-non-archived-agent bound below. See the route's 503 response for that bound and for the enhanced path's stricter, never-partial failure behaviour.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page to return, 1-indexed. IGNORED when agent_id is present: the response then always reports page 1, since there is at most one row to page over. Unpaged calls return the first page (24 agents), the same as the endpoint's previous behaviour.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: The number of Agent rows per page (maximum 100, shared with the portfolio list route's per_page). When agent_id is present this stops controlling how many rows are returned (at most one), but the requested value (or the default of 24 if omitted) is still reported back unchanged in the response's pagination.per_page. Unpaged calls return the first page (24 agents), the same as the endpoint's previous behaviour.

parameters.name: agent_id
parameters.description: Restrict the response to this one Agent's row (page 1 of at most 1 total; page/per_page paging is IGNORED, see page/per_page). This is a collection filter, not a per-agent lookup: an unknown or inaccessible id returns 200, never 404, so the parameter carries no existence oracle. Unknown and inaccessible are INDISTINGUISHABLE: the response is exactly the empty-fleet shape -- `agents: []`, `failed_agent_ids: []`, `validate_first: []`, `summary.total: 0` with every counts_by_verdict member 0, and `pagination: {page: 1, per_page: <the requested or default per_page>, total: 0, total_pages: 0, has_next: false, has_prev: false}` -- and the requested id is never echoed anywhere in the response.

parameters.name: verdict
parameters.description: Restrict returned rows to agents whose verdict is one of the given values (repeatable query parameter, e.g. ?verdict=STAY&verdict=INTERVENE_QUALITY -- OR within this parameter). A single comma-separated value (e.g. ?verdict=STAY,INTERVENE_QUALITY) is REJECTED as invalid, not parsed as a list. A repeated identical value (e.g. ?verdict=STAY&verdict=STAY) is accepted and de-duplicated. Combines by AND with stage, deployment_stage, search and agent_id. Applies before pagination: pagination.total is the count after this filter, not the project's unfiltered total. An unknown/invalid verdict value yields the existing 400 envelope (see the route's 400 response); the invalid value is never echoed back.

parameters.name: stage
parameters.description: Restrict returned rows to agents whose evaluation-progress stage (agent_readiness_common_schema.json ProcessStage: NO_RUNS | RUNS_RECORDED | EVALUATION_COMPLETED -- the same evaluation-progress vocabulary as the existing readiness-portfolio stage filter) is one of the given values (repeatable: OR within this parameter). A comma-separated value is REJECTED. A repeated identical value is accepted and de-duplicated. Combines by AND with verdict, deployment_stage, search and agent_id. Applies before pagination: pagination.total is the filtered count. An unknown/invalid value yields the existing 400 envelope, never echoed.

parameters.name: deployment_stage
parameters.description: Restrict returned rows to agents whose manager-declared deployment_stage (agent_posture_schema.json DeploymentStage, reusing the agent-deployment Environment enum: development | staging | production | testing) is one of the given values (repeatable: OR within this parameter). A comma-separated value is REJECTED. A repeated identical value is accepted and de-duplicated. An agent with no declared posture (NONE_DECLARED) matches no deployment_stage value -- the same no-default rule as agent_posture_schema.json's AgentPosture. Combines by AND with verdict, stage, search and agent_id. Applies before pagination: pagination.total is the filtered count. An unknown/invalid value yields the existing 400 envelope, never echoed.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Case-folded substring filter on agent_name. The machine-checkable bound is on the RAW query value: at most 200 characters (no minimum -- an empty string is a syntactically valid raw value). Semantically: the raw value is trimmed of leading/trailing whitespace before matching; a value that trims to empty (blank or whitespace-only, including an empty raw string) is treated as ABSENT (no filter applied at all -- not an error, and it does NOT trigger the enhanced path, see the operation description). A non-blank trimmed value matches as a literal, non-wildcard, casefolded substring of agent_name: the characters %, _ and \ are matched literally, never interpreted as SQL/LIKE wildcards or escapes. Combines by AND with verdict, stage, deployment_stage and agent_id. Applies before pagination: pagination.total is the filtered count. A raw value over 200 characters is the only way this parameter alone yields the existing 400 envelope; the value is never echoed.

parameters.name: include_project_summary
parameters.description: When true, the response's optional project_summary is populated: its total and counts_by_verdict cover every caller-visible, non-archived agent in the project, independent of every filter on this request -- including agent_id, verdict, stage, deployment_stage and search. project_summary is identical whether agent_id is omitted, matches a known agent, or matches none. Defaults to false (project_summary omitted from the response); an explicit include_project_summary=false does NOT trigger the enhanced path (see the operation description). Only a single literal true|false value is accepted; a duplicate occurrence or any other value is a 400, never echoed. The required, page-scoped summary is unaffected and always reflects only the agents returned on this page. See the route's 503 response for the bound on this computation (and on stage/verdict/deployment_stage/search) at 500 caller-visible, non-archived agents, and for the never-partial computation-failure rule.

400.description: Invalid pagination, filter (verdict/stage/deployment_stage), search, or include_project_summary parameters

503.description: Returned only for a request on the enhanced path (see the operation description's precise ENHANCED PATH definition: verdict/stage/deployment_stage present, a non-blank search, or include_project_summary=true). Two distinct triggers, both fail-closed and never partial: (1) the project has more than 500 caller-visible, non-archived agents -- computing filtered rows and/or project_summary requires evaluating every one of them, so above that bound the request fails closed instead of ever returning a truncated or partial pagination.total or project_summary; (2) ANY per-agent computation failure while evaluating that same caller-visible, non-archived universe (the same kind of per-agent read failure that the page-only path tolerates and records in failed_agent_ids) -- on the enhanced path this fails the WHOLE request closed instead of omitting that one agent, because a filtered count or a project_summary that silently excluded a failed agent would misstate the total. The pre-existing page-only path (no enhanced-path trigger present, including a blank/whitespace-only search or an explicit include_project_summary=false) is unaffected by both triggers and keeps its existing failed_agent_ids partial-failure tolerance. Body: the same closed, content-free error envelope as the route's 400/401/403 responses (agent_readiness_error_schema.json), success=false with message 'Service unavailable', error 'service_unavailable', error_code 'service_unavailable'. Retry without any enhanced-path parameter to use the unaffected page-only path, or narrow scope and retry the enhanced request.
